input.reasoning_summary:
After investigating potential challenges to the initial verdict, all three hypotheses were refuted:

H1 (Cost reductions as primary driver): REFUTED. Evidence E7 shows that Family of Apps costs and expenses actually INCREASED in Q1 2026 compared to Q1 2025. Employee compensation increased from $9,031M to $12,079M, and other costs increased from $11,106M to $16,930M. Evidence E2 explicitly states the increase was "driven by higher advertising revenue which was partially offset by an increase in costs and expenses." Cost reductions did not contribute to operating income growth; rather, costs increased and partially offset the revenue gains.

H2 (Non-advertising revenue as primary driver): REFUTED. Evidence E3 shows that of the $14.01 billion FoA revenue increase, advertising revenue contributed $13.63 billion (from E4), meaning advertising accounted for approximately 97% of the revenue growth. The filing states the increase was "almost entirely driven by advertising revenue."

H3 (One-time items as primary driver): REFUTED. Evidence E2 clearly attributes the operating income growth to "higher advertising revenue" as the driver. While E1 mentions a one-time tax benefit of $8.03 billion, this affects the provision for income taxes, not operating income. Operating income is calculated before tax items, so this one-time benefit is irrelevant to the claim about operating income drivers.

The initial verdict remains SUPPORTED. The filing explicitly and consistently states that Family of Apps operating income growth in Q1 2026 was driven by advertising revenue growth.
